newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guatemalan peace talks start anew in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan peace talks start anew in Mexico.

text.p: Guatemalan officials and left-wing rebels started a new round of peace talks in the Mexican capital on Friday and Spain offered to host the signing of an agreement this year.

The Spanish prime minister Jose Maria Aznar told a news conference during a state visit to Mexico that he had accepted a request from both sides in the 35-year conflict to host the signing of a partial peace accord in Madrid.

He said the agreement was aimed at the reintegration of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) rebels into political life. A final accord, ordering a ceasefire, is due to be signed in Oslo also before the end of 1996, government peace negotiator Gustavo Porras said.
The two sides in Mexico renewed discussions on Friday on the question of strengthening civilian government in Guatemala and reducing the role of the army.
Porras said before leaving Guatemala on Thursday that he hoped the issue could be wrapped up by September 15, the anniversary of Guatemala's Independence Day.
Some 100,000 people have died in the civil war and more than 40,000 have disappeared.
